scenarioStory.history: Patient was working near a propane tank that exploded, throwing him several feet. He has an actively bleeding shrapnel wound to the right thigh, partial-thickness burns to his face and forearms, and reports ringing in his ears with difficulty hearing questions. He is anxious and repeatedly asks crew to speak up.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 33-year-old male with an actively bleeding right thigh wound from shrapnel, partial-thickness burns to the face and forearms, and apparent hearing loss/tinnitus from the blast overpressure. He is alert but anxious and has difficulty hearing questions. → Massive hemorrhage controlled first: Crew immediately applies a tourniquet to the actively bleeding right thigh wound before addressing the burns or hearing complaint, following the MARCH massive-hemorrhage-first priority, then continues the primary survey. → Breath sounds reassessed on right: With hemorrhage controlled, the crew reassesses breathing and finds progressively diminished breath sounds on the right with rising respiratory distress, tachycardia, and borderline hypotension — early tension physiology from blast barotrauma — and performs needle decompression while managing the burns and IV fluids. → Decompression relieves pressure, packaged for transport: Needle decompression relieves the tension physiology; breath sounds and vitals improve. The crew completes burn dressing, secures IV fluids, and packages the patient with a clearly marked tourniquet for transport to a trauma center with burn capability.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Explosion victim with bleeding leg wound, burns, and hearing loss

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 33-year-old male with an actively bleeding right thigh wound from shrapnel, partial-thickness burns to the face and forearms, and apparent hearing loss/tinnitus from the blast overpressure. He is alert but anxious and has difficulty hearing questions.

scenarioEvents.name: Massive hemorrhage controlled first
scenarioEvents.description: Crew immediately applies a tourniquet to the actively bleeding right thigh wound before addressing the burns or hearing complaint, following the MARCH massive-hemorrhage-first priority, then continues the primary survey.
relatedChecklist: Perform MARCH primary survey prioritizing hemorrhage control over burns/hearing loss
Apply commercial tourniquet 2-3 in proximal to right thigh wound; mark placement time
Continually reassess for blast lung injury and possible airway burn

scenarioEvents.name: Breath sounds reassessed on right
scenarioEvents.description: With hemorrhage controlled, the crew reassesses breathing and finds progressively diminished breath sounds on the right with rising respiratory distress, tachycardia, and borderline hypotension — early tension physiology from blast barotrauma — and performs needle decompression while managing the burns and IV fluids.
relatedChecklist: Needle decompression right 2nd ICS midclavicular line for tension pneumothorax
Establish IV access; administer NS per Burns Guideline given TBSA and shock signs
Rapid total-body exposure exam including log roll; keep patient warm

scenarioEvents.name: Decompression relieves pressure, packaged for transport
scenarioEvents.description: Needle decompression relieves the tension physiology; breath sounds and vitals improve. The crew completes burn dressing, secures IV fluids, and packages the patient with a clearly marked tourniquet for transport to a trauma center with burn capability.
relatedChecklist: Transport to trauma center with burn capability per field triage guideline; minimize scene time
Reassess vitals, breath sounds, and tourniquet serially en route

scenarioEvents.name: Tourniquet delayed for burns/hearing
scenarioEvents.description: The crew is drawn to the dramatic-looking burns and the patient's hearing loss/confusion, delaying tourniquet application on the actively bleeding thigh wound. Ongoing blood loss drives the patient into hemorrhagic shock.
relatedChecklist: Recognize hemorrhagic shock; apply tourniquet immediately, consider TXA

scenarioEvents.name: Decompression delayed despite worsening signs
scenarioEvents.description: The crew continues focusing on burn dressing and IV access while the patient's respiratory distress, hypotension, and tracheal deviation worsen without needle decompression — a progressing, untreated tension pneumothorax.
relatedChecklist: Recognize tension pneumothorax; needle decompress right 2nd ICS immediately
